title: Vigil held for disabled man who died in arrest
article: Friends and family gathered Monday night to honour Charles McGillivary, a mentally disabled man who died one week earlier following his arrest by Toronto police.
Hundreds gathered at Christie Pits Park, not far from the spot where McGillivary died. Many there described him as a gentle child trapped in a man's body.
Local MPP Rosario Marchese attended Monday's vigil and promised to press police for answers about McGillvary's death and details about how officers are trained to handle people with disabilities.
McGillivary, 45, was mentally disabled and left unable to speak since being struck by a car when he was four years old.
McGillivary and his mother, Ann, were out for a walk at about 8 p.m. on Aug. 1. Charles stopped to get some food at a Bloor Street pizza parlour.

According to Ontario's Special Investigations Unit, which is investigating McGillivary's death, he collapsed during an interaction with police. The SIU is automatically called in when police involvement in a situation results in death or serious injury.
